'''Joseph Daniel Harris''' (born August 17, 1951) is the Higgins Professor of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="Harris">{{cite web |title=Joseph Harris |url=https://pll.harvard.edu/instructor/joseph-harris |access-date=25 October 2024 |department=Professional and Lifelong Learning |website=Harvard University |date=28 February 2018 }}</ref> He specializes in the field of [[algebraic geometry]]. After earning an AB from [[Harvard College]] he continued at Harvard to study for a PhD under [[Phillip Griffiths]].

==Work==
During the 1980s, he was on the faculty of [[Brown University]], moving to Harvard in 1988.<ref name=Harris/> He served as chair of the department at Harvard from 2002 to 2005.  His work is characterized by its classical geometric flavor: he has claimed that nothing he thinks about could not have been imagined by the [[Italian geometers]] of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and that if he has had greater success than them, it is because he has access to better tools.{{Citation needed|date=September 2009}}

Harris is well known for several of his books on algebraic geometry, notable for their informal presentations:
* ''Principles of Algebraic Geometry'' {{ISBN|978-0-471-05059-9}}, with Phillip Griffiths<ref>{{cite journal|author=[[Joseph Lipman|Lipman, Joseph]]|title=Review: ''Principles of algebraic geometry'', by Phillip Godwin, and Joseph Harris|year=1980|volume=2|issue=1|pages=197–200|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1980-02-01/S0273-0979-1980-14717-5/S0273-0979-1980-14717-5.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1980-14717-5|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''Geometry of Algebraic Curves, Vol. 1'' {{ISBN|978-0-387-90997-4}}, with [[Enrico Arbarello]], [[Maurizio Cornalba]], and Phillip Griffiths
* {{Citation | title=Representation Theory, A First Course | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | location=Berlin, New York | series=[[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]] | isbn=978-0-387-97495-8 |mr=1153249 | year=1991 | volume=129 | author=William Fulton, Joe Harris. | doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-0979-9}}, with [[William Fulton (mathematician)|William Fulton]]
* {{cite book | last=Harris | first=Joe | title = Algebraic Geometry, A First Course | year=1992| publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer Science]] | url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9780387977164 | isbn=978-0-387-97716-4}}
* {{Citation | title=The Geometry of Schemes | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | location=Berlin, New York | series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics | isbn=978-0-387-98638-8 |mr=1730819 | year=2000 | volume=197 | author=David Eisenbud, Joe Harris.}}, with [[David Eisenbud]]
*{{cite book| title=3264 and All That: A Second Course in Algebraic Geometry|author=[[David Eisenbud]], Joseph Harris (2016)|date=14 April 2016|publisher= [[Cambridge University Press]]| isbn=978-1107602724}}
* ''Moduli of Curves'' {{ISBN|978-0-387-98438-4}}, with [[Ian Morrison (mathematician)|Ian Morrison]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Ciliberto, Ciro|title=Review: ''Moduli of curves'', by J. Harris and I. Morrison|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=1999|volume=36|issue=4|pages=499–503|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1999-36-04/S0273-0979-99-00791-0/S0273-0979-99-00791-0.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-99-00791-0|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''[[Fat Chance: Probability from 0 to 1]]'', with [[Benedict Gross]] and [[Emily Riehl]], 2019<ref>{{cite book|title=Fat Chance: Probability from 0 to 1|last1=Gross|first1=Benedict|author1-link=Benedict Gross|last2=Harris|first2=Joe|author2-link=Joe Harris (mathematician)|first3=Emily|last3=Riehl|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2019}} Reviews:
*{{cite journal|first=Mark|last=Bollman|title=none|journal=Mathematical Reviews|mr=3931738}}
*{{cite journal|first=Ludwig|last=Paditz|title=none|journal=zbMATH|zbl=1423.00005}}
*{{cite journal|last=Nespolo|first=Massimo|date=November 2019|doi=10.1107/s1600576719014055|issue=6|journal=Journal of Applied Crystallography|pages=1467–1468|title=none|volume=52|doi-access=free}}</ref>
As of 2018, Harris has supervised 50 PhD students, including [[Lucia Caporaso]], [[Brendan Hassett]], [[James McKernan]], [[Rahul Pandharipande]], [[Zvezdelina Stankova]], and [[Ravi Vakil]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=18748|title=Joseph Harris - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2018-05-01}}</ref>
